statements.proposition: The change keeps standalone Redis behaviour unchanged (backward compatible).
statements.label: TRUE
statements.note: Settled by diff inspection of the standalone path and caller search, not by running against Redis; the only observable difference for standalone is that registration (and any registration error) now happens on first request instead of in __init__.
evidence: PR diff: the standalone branch `return _redis_client.register_script(script)` in async_register_script is unchanged context; only the cluster branch (script_load/evalsha) gained await
git grep at head: the only caller of async_register_script is parallel_request_limiter_v3._initialize_scripts, which now awaits it; no sync callers remain
Scripts are now registered lazily on first use (_initialize_scripts) for standalone as well; the registered objects and their call sites are the same, and no end-to-end Redis run was done
